brief: UAE: Emaar's revenue from malls, retail and commercial leasing rose 10% to Dh5.2bn in the first nine months at about 98% occupancy, while its hotel occupancy fell to 63% from 80%; it has also proposed buying out the rest of Emaar Development at Dh15 a share.
Members: Majid Al Futtaim brought its SHARE rewards programme to Carrefour's 35 stores in Kenya, where about 1.4 million MyClub members move across once they accept the new terms.

2027 Directory: Friday's check of 16 listings found 7 to change, among them 'Masat Mall', which is Hamat's Masar Mall in Makkah, two cards for one Pixel Plaza, Silicon Central trading since 2021 and Jeddah Vibes trading by Q1 2026; 8 could not be confirmed from owners' sources.

Also new: Orbis Group's first mall, Jurt in Astana (9,000 sq m leasable), was due to open on 24 Oct; Dubai's RTA pilots nol-Jaywan cards on the national payment scheme from November; and Instacart is winding down its Caper smart carts.

Quiet day: two verified items were dated 5 Nov; Leejam and Alsaif Gallery put the 2027 Saudi utility tariffs at 1.5-2% and about 0.3% of cost of revenue, and Cenomi Centers had still not filed its Q3 results by 6 Nov.
weekly_brief: Week 45 (2 to 6 November): 36 findings and 9 library documents across five editions, and the fourth Friday check of directory listings (16 listings).

Saudi pipeline: PIF's Saudi Downtown Company launched Al Khobar Downtown, an 829,000 sqm waterfront scheme with more than 139,000 sqm of retail and dining around the mall Cenomi is developing; Cenomi signed a SAR 825m design-and-build contract for the Madinah Downtown mall and offices; and Riyadh Municipality opened bidding on its first joint land investment, a 30,000 sqm mixed-use plot.

Results: Emaar's mall and retail leasing revenue rose 10% to Dh5.2bn in nine months at about 98% occupancy while hotel occupancy fell to 63%; Seef Properties' nine-month profit fell 30% on weaker leisure and spending; Jabal Omar swung to a Q3 loss as land-sale gains dropped out; Emaar The Economic City's loss widened; and Cenomi Centers had still not filed by 6 Nov.

Tenants and new schemes: M&S will open its largest Foodhall outside the UK at Dubai Festival City in December; OVS took direct control of its UAE stores; Sports Direct entered Africa at two Nairobi malls; Waitrose is the first tenant of DMCC's Uptown Place; Fashion House Group will develop an outlet at Grand Uptown Mall in New October City; Edamah and Kanoo will develop Pier 1890 in Manama; and Bishkek's Ala-Too market opened for the Madina bazaar's traders.

Members and loyalty: Magrabi agreed to buy Dubai Optical and its 15 Dubai Optical-branded UAE stores, and Majid Al Futtaim brought its SHARE rewards programme to Carrefour Kenya and its 1.4 million MyClub members.

Spending and service: Turkish mall sales per sqm rose 29.7% in September, in line with inflation, led by entertainment; UAE gold jewellery demand fell 29% in Q3; the UAE's Global Star Rating covered 179 government service channels; and Dubai launched an Access Club for repeat visitors and will pilot nol-Jaywan payment cards.

AI and retail technology: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for about $17bn, and Instacart is winding down its Caper smart carts; Amazon opened its Alexa for Shopping agent to outside merchants; Salesforce agreed to buy voice AI firm Cresta; Abu Dhabi signed agreements with OpenAI; and holiday surveys show shoppers want to approve any purchase an AI makes for them.

2027 Directory: sheet 10 gained the Madinah Downtown and Al Khobar Downtown malls (Add to pipeline), Pier 1890, Uptown Place and the Grand Uptown Mall outlet (Watch), and the Ala-Too market, Sarit Centre, Galleria Mall and Astana's Jurt (Check first); Friday's check changed 7 of 16 listings, including two cards for one Pixel Plaza, Silicon Central trading since 2021 and 'Masat Mall' being Hamat's Masar Mall, while 8 could not be confirmed from owners' sources.

findings.title: Emaar's mall and retail leasing revenue rises 10% to Dh5.2bn in nine months at about 98% occupancy, as hotel occupancy falls to 63%
findings.summary:
Emaar Properties' revenue rose 13% to Dh37.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with property sales of Dh34.7 billion and a revenue backlog of Dh158.8 billion at the end of September, up 6%. Revenue from shopping malls, retail and commercial leasing rose 10% to Dh5.2 billion, with occupancy of about 98%, while average hotel occupancy fell to 63% from 80% a year earlier.

A day earlier Emaar proposed a cash offer of Dh15 a share for the Emaar Development shares it does not already own. Gulf News says the offer is still subject to board approval, while The National reports that the board has approved it and that Emaar plans to delist the unit.
findings.why: The owner of The Dubai Mall grew leasing revenue at near-full occupancy while hotel occupancy fell sharply, a Q3 benchmark for Dubai mall landlords.

findings.title: Majid Al Futtaim brings its SHARE rewards programme to Carrefour's 35 stores in Kenya
findings.summary: Majid Al Futtaim launched its SHARE rewards programme in Kenya on 5 Nov inside the existing Carrefour app, with points earned on in-store and online Carrefour purchases at a base rate of 0.25%. About 1.4 million members of Carrefour's MyClub programme move to SHARE automatically once they accept the updated terms and set their marketing preferences; Carrefour has 35 stores in Kenya, mostly in Nairobi. Launch offers include up to 4,500 welcome points, double base points on SHARE Mondays and 20% back in points on eligible birthday purchases. SHARE already runs in the UAE, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Oman and has more than 15 million members.
findings.why: A member is moving a large loyalty base onto its regional platform inside a retailer's app, with fresh consent, a live case for MECSC's loyalty and CX content.

findings.title: Orbis Group moves into retail real estate with Jurt, a two-floor mall in Astana led by a farm-food hall
findings.summary: Forbes Kazakhstan reported on 22 Oct that Orbis Group, the diversified holding owned by Farrukh and Sukhrab Makhmudov, planned the official opening of Jurt, its first mall, on Astana's right bank for 24 October, with 17,000 sq m of total area, 9,000 sq m of leasable area and more than 100 units on two floors. Tenants include a 1,200 sq m Fresh Market farm-food hall modelled on Almaty's Green Bazaar, KFC, Hardee's, Dodo Pizza, NAVAT and the Yondo family entertainment centre. Farrukh Makhmudov calls Jurt a new business line and says the group will judge the format's economics before expanding to other regions; no dated report confirms the opening yet.
findings.why: A new Kazakh mall developer is testing a farm-market-led community format it may take to other regions, a new property for the Central Asia pipeline.

findings.company: Roads and Transport Authority (RTA); Al Etihad Payments
findings.title: Dubai's RTA will pilot nol-Jaywan cards, joining the nol transit card to the UAE's national Jaywan payment scheme, from November
findings.summary: Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority has signed an agreement with Al Etihad Payments, a subsidiary of the Central Bank of the UAE, to introduce new-generation nol cards in phases that combine the nol transport system with Jaywan, the UAE's national card payment scheme. A pilot starts in November 2026 on RTA public transport, including taxis and public parking; cards are activated and managed on Android and iOS phones, and wider use is planned across public and private transport and online booking platforms in the UAE. Cardholders get access to more than 120 promotional offers and discounts. RTA has not given a date for general availability, named the businesses that will accept the cards or said whether existing nol cards must be replaced.
findings.why: A national-scheme payment card with built-in offers, carried by Dubai's daily commuters, could become a payment and promotions channel for malls and retailers once merchant acceptance is defined.

findings.title: Instacart will wind down its Caper smart-cart business by mid-2027 and move in-store work to software and AI
findings.summary: Instacart said on 26 Oct that it is winding down its Caper Cart smart-cart business, to be completed by the end of Q2 2027, because 'retailer adoption has not scaled quickly enough to justify our continued investment'. Its next in-store phase centres on software, data and AI that report on store performance, including a live view of stores for grocers and consumer brands and Arpalus, an AI tool bought this summer that lets staff record product levels with a smartphone. The decision, disclosed in a company update and a regulatory filing, came days before DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart (see 2 Nov).
findings.why: A leading smart-cart provider is retreating to software, a signal for GCC grocers and mall operators weighing checkout hardware against store-wide data and AI.

findings.company: Hamat Holding; Umm Al-Qura for Development and Construction
findings.title: 'Masat Mall' is Hamat's Masar Mall in Makkah, and its owners publish neither the printed GLA nor a Q1 2027 opening
findings.summary: Hamat's own page names the scheme Masar Mall, an upcoming mall at the western entrance of the Masar destination in Makkah, opposite the Haramain High-Speed Railway station, spanning 71,000 sqm with more than 130,000 sqm of retail space; neither figure is labelled GLA. Umm Al-Qura for Development and Construction, owner of Masar, announced in January 2022 that Hamat Holding would develop and operate the mall, with up to SAR 2.7bn of investment and completion in 2026. Hamat's Cityscape item of 25 May 2025 still describes it as upcoming, with no date. The directory prints 'Masat Mall' with a GLA of 50,650 sqm and a Q1 2027 opening.
findings.why: Corrects the name, size and partner of a member's pipeline listing and flags an opening date that no owner source supports.

findings.entity: Silicon Central Mall, Dubai Silicon Oasis
findings.title: Silicon Central has traded since its 2021 soft opening, and its owner publishes 81,500 sqm GLA, not 77,521 sqm
findings.summary: Line Investments & Property, the mall development and management arm of LuLu Group International, announced the soft opening of Silicon Central in Dubai Silicon Oasis in a release carried by Zawya on 1 Sep 2021, with a total GLA of 81,500 sqm. Zawya's own 2021 report says the mall opened its doors that week, with a 9,000 square-metre LuLu flagship store. The directory still prints it as a new mall with 77,521 sqm GLA and no owner or opening year.
findings.why: Moves a trading member mall out of the pipeline and corrects its size and owner.

findings.entity: The Atrium, Uptown Tower, Uptown Dubai

DMCC's release of 3 Nov 2026 covers a separate building: Uptown Place, two towers next to Uptown Tower with 82,000 sq ft of retail space in 18 units, due to open in Q1 2028. The directory prints The Atrium as an upcoming community centre of 6,157 sqm due in 2024.

findings.title: Agaoglu Cekmeköy Park in Istanbul belongs to the Agaoglu Group, with ECE Türkiye as manager, not owner
findings.summary: ECE's release says ECE Türkiye has taken over asset and property management, leasing and concept optimisation for Agaoglu Cekmeköy Park, the shopping centre of the Agaoglu Group of Companies' mixed-use scheme in Çekmeköy, Istanbul, which also includes 739 homes. The centre has 25,000 sq m of rental space and around 100 stores, and the group is investing more than 200 million euros in the whole scheme. The release, which ECE's files date to February 2024, gave an end-2024 opening; no owner source found confirms that the centre has opened.
findings.why: The card names the manager as owner, lacks a country, city and year, and its upcoming status rests on an end-2024 opening that has passed.
